1: But, besides personal inspection, he has other assurance of the good qualities of the man before him; at a late hour on the night before he held a communication with Don Gregorio, who has recommended him. The haciendado had reported what Crozier said, that Harry Blew was an able seaman, thoroughly trustworthy, and competent to take charge of a ship, either as first or second officer.
7: With Crozier's endorsement thus vicariously conveyed, the ex-man-o'-war's man has no need to say a word for himself. Nor does Captain Lantanas call for it. He only puts some professional questions, less inquisitorially than as a matter of form.
11: "The Senor Silvestre advises me that you wish to serve in my ship. Can you take a lunar?"
12: "Well, capten; I hev squinted through a quadrant afores now, an' can take a sight; tho' I arn't much up to loonars. But if there's a good chronometer aboard, I won't let a ship run very far out of her reck'nin'."
14: "You can keep a log-book, I suppose?"
16: "I dare say I can. I've larned to write, so 'st might be read; though my fist ain't much to be bragged about."
19: "That will do," rejoins the skipper, contentedly. "Now, Senor Enrique-- I see that's your name--answer me in all candour. Do you think you are capable of acting as piloto?"
20: "By that you mean mate, I take it?"
22: "Well, capten; 'tain't for me to talk big o' myself. But I've been over thirty year 'board a British man-o'-war--more'n one o' 'em--an' if I wan't able to go mate in a merchanter, I ought to be condemned to be cook's scullion for the rest o' my days. If your honour thinks me worthy o' bein' made first officer o' the Condor, I'll answer for it she won't stray far out o' her course while my watch be on."
27: "Bueno! Senor Enrique--B--blee. What is it?" asks the Chilian, re-opening the note, and vainly endeavouring to pronounce the Saxon surname.
30:
"Ah, Bloo--azul, esta?"

"No, capten. Not that sort o' blue. In Spanish, my name has a different significance. It means, as we say o' a gale after it's blowed past--it `blew.' When it's been a big un, we say it `blew great guns.' Now ye understan'?"
31: "Yes; perfectly. Well, Senor Bloo, to come to an understanding about the other matter. I'm willing to take you as my first officer, if you don't object to the wages I intend offering you--fifty dollars a month, and everything found."
33:
"Basta! When will it be convenient for you to enter in your duties?"

"For that matter, this minute. I only need to go ashore to get my kit. When that's stowed, I'll be ready to tackle on to work."
34: "Muy bien! senor; you can take my boat for it. And if you see any sailors who want to join, I authorise you to engage them at double the usual wages. I wish to get away as soon as a crew can be shipped. But when you come back we'll talk more about it. Call at Senor Silvestre's office, and tell him he needn't look for me till a later hour. Say I've some business that detains me aboard. Hasta Luego!"
37: Thus courteously concluding, the Chilian skipper returns to his cabin, leaving the newly appointed piloto free to look after his own affairs.
